column1: ACTC1|AD|HCM;DCM;LV noncompaction|Cardiac alpha-actin forms the thin filament. Disease-associated variants can alter force generation and produce hypertrophic, dilated, or noncompaction phenotypes.|Interpret against the specific cardiomyopathy phenotype and family segregation.|hcm|

ACTN2|AD|HCM;DCM;Skeletal myopathy|Alpha-actinin-2 anchors the sarcomere at the Z-disc. Pathogenic variants cause a spectrum of cardiac disease, sometimes with skeletal muscle involvement.|A core addition in the PDF; the 2025 HCM reappraisal supports definitive disease validity.|hcm|

ALPK3|AD / AR|HCM;Pediatric cardiomyopathy|ALPK3 supports cardiomyocyte structure. Heterozygous loss-of-function variants can cause HCM; biallelic disease often presents earlier and more severely.|Confirm zygosity and mechanism. The HCM reappraisal distinguishes strong dominant from definitive recessive evidence.|hcm|

BAG3|AD|DCM;Myofibrillar myopathy|BAG3 helps maintain protein quality in cardiac muscle. Loss-of-function variants are associated with dilated cardiomyopathy; certain variants produce severe multisystem myopathy.|Consider skeletal weakness, neuropathy, and variant-specific syndromic presentations.|dcm|

CAV3|AD / AR; phenotype-dependent|Caveolinopathy;Muscle disease;Reported cardiac phenotypes|Caveolin-3 organizes muscle membrane caveolae. It is retained in both source panels, but its skeletal muscle disease association must be separated from proposed cardiac associations.|Do not infer a monogenic arrhythmia diagnosis from panel inclusion. Review the exact gene-disease pair.|lqts|Congenital LQTS evidence is limited or disputed; isolated cardiomyopathy claims also require careful review.

CRYAB|AD / AR|Myofibrillar myopathy;Cataracts;Reported cardiomyopathy|Alpha-B crystallin protects structural proteins under stress. Some disease-associated variants produce myofibrillar muscle disease with cardiac involvement.|Ask about cataracts and skeletal weakness; isolated HCM evidence should be reviewed separately.|dcm|Retained broad-panel gene; evidence depends on the syndrome and variant mechanism.

CSRP3|Semidominant|HCM;Reported DCM|Muscle LIM protein participates in sarcomere organization and stress sensing. CSRP3-related HCM can show a dosage effect, with more severe disease in biallelic individuals.|The 2025 reappraisal supports definitive semidominant HCM; consider allele dosage and segregation.|hcm|

DES|AD / AR|DCM;Restrictive CM;Conduction disease;Myofibrillar myopathy|Desmin connects the muscle contractile apparatus to the cell scaffold. Desminopathy may combine cardiomyopathy, atrioventricular block, arrhythmia, and skeletal muscle weakness.|Conduction disease can be prominent. Review rhythm findings alongside imaging and neuromuscular assessment.|dcm|

DMD|X-linked|DCM;Duchenne / Becker dystrophy;Affected female carriers|Dystrophin stabilizes the muscle cell membrane. Dystrophinopathy may cause dilated cardiomyopathy before, or with little, skeletal muscle disease; heterozygous females may be affected.|Require validated exon deletion/duplication analysis as well as sequencing. Assess cardiac risk in female relatives.|dmd|

DSC2|AD / AR|Arrhythmogenic CM;Ventricular arrhythmia|Desmocollin-2 is a desmosomal adhesion protein. Pathogenic variants can weaken mechanical coupling and cause arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy with right, left, or biventricular involvement.|Interpret with ACM criteria, imaging, rhythm phenotype, and family segregation.|acm|

DSG2|AD / AR|Arrhythmogenic CM;DCM;Ventricular arrhythmia|Desmoglein-2 links neighboring cardiac cells through desmosomes. Disease-associated variants can produce ventricular arrhythmia and progressive myocardial dysfunction.|Electrical disease may precede obvious ventricular dysfunction; assess both structural and rhythm features.|acm|

DSP|AD / AR|Arrhythmogenic CM;LV fibrosis;Cardiocutaneous syndrome|Desmoplakin anchors desmosomes to the cytoskeleton. DSP cardiomyopathy often affects the left ventricle and may present with myocardial injury episodes, fibrosis, and ventricular arrhythmia.|Review CMR fibrosis and myocarditis-like episodes. Woolly hair or palmoplantar keratoderma suggests a cardiocutaneous phenotype.|acm|

FHL1|X-linked|HCM;Reducing-body myopathy;Emery-Dreifuss phenotype|FHL1 participates in muscle structure and signaling. Its disorders may combine hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with weakness, muscle hypertrophy, or contractures.|A neuromuscular examination and X-linked pedigree can clarify an apparently isolated cardiac presentation.|dcm|

FHOD3|AD|HCM|FHOD3 regulates actin organization in cardiomyocytes. Pathogenic variants can disrupt sarcomere maintenance and cause hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.|New in the PDF; the 2025 ClinGen HCM reappraisal supports definitive validity. Check variant mechanism and segregation.|hcm|

FLNC|AD|DCM;Arrhythmogenic CM;HCM;Myofibrillar myopathy|Filamin-C links and stabilizes the muscle cytoskeleton. Truncating variants are associated with arrhythmogenic dilated disease, whereas some missense variants cause hypertrophic or myopathic phenotypes.|Mechanism matters: do not transfer a truncating-variant risk profile to every FLNC variant.|dcm|

GLA|X-linked|Fabry disease;LVH / HCM mimic;Renal disease;Neuropathic pain|Alpha-galactosidase A deficiency causes Fabry disease, a potentially treatable storage disorder that can mimic sarcomeric HCM. Late cardiac-predominant disease may lack classic systemic signs.|Correlate the variant with biochemical testing. Normal enzyme activity does not exclude disease in females; confirmed disease merits specialist therapy assessment.|fabry|

JPH2|AD / AR; phenotype-dependent|HCM;Early-onset DCM|Junctophilin-2 maintains the junction between the cell membrane and sarcoplasmic reticulum, enabling coordinated calcium release during contraction.|Evaluate inheritance and phenotype carefully; dominant HCM and recessive early-onset disease require different interpretation.|hcm|HCM evidence is moderate in the 2025 reappraisal; review the exact variant and disease pair.

JUP|AD / AR|Arrhythmogenic CM;Naxos disease|Plakoglobin is a desmosomal component. Biallelic pathogenic variants cause Naxos disease, combining arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy with woolly hair and palmoplantar keratoderma.|Examine skin and hair and establish zygosity; monoallelic findings need phenotype-specific review.|acm|

LMNA|AD|DCM;AV block;Atrial / ventricular arrhythmia|Lamin A/C supports the nuclear envelope. LMNA-related cardiomyopathy often begins with conduction disease or arrhythmia before substantial left ventricular dilation or systolic impairment.|A confirmed pathogenic variant can inform specialist arrhythmic risk assessment and family surveillance. Consider neuromuscular features and a three-generation pedigree.|lmna|

MYBPC3|AD; biallelic disease possible|HCM;Severe early-onset CM|Cardiac myosin-binding protein C regulates sarcomere contraction. Loss-of-function variants are a major cause of inherited HCM with age-dependent and variable expression.|A normal assessment in a young relative does not exclude later expression. Consider biallelic disease in severe infantile presentations.|hcm|

MYH7|AD|HCM;DCM;LV noncompaction;Skeletal myopathy|Beta-myosin heavy chain drives muscle contraction. Specific pathogenic variants produce different cardiac and skeletal muscle phenotypes.|Variant location and mechanism are important; a truncating variant is not automatically a typical MYH7-HCM allele.|hcm|

MYL2|AD / AR|HCM;Infantile cardioskeletal disease|Myosin regulatory light chain modulates sarcomere contraction. Dominant pathogenic variants can cause HCM; recessive disease can have severe early cardiac and skeletal involvement.|Match zygosity and variant class to the phenotype, particularly in infants.|hcm|

MYL3|AD / AR|HCM|Myosin essential light chain contributes to force generation. Disease-associated variants can produce hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, including biallelic presentations.|Review allele dosage, segregation, and the specific variant evidence.|hcm|

NEXN|AD / AR|DCM;Early-onset cardiomyopathy|Nexilin supports cardiac membrane and cytoskeletal organization. Rare NEXN variants have been associated with dilated cardiomyopathy, including severe biallelic presentations.|The 2026 DCM reassessment upgraded the evidence. The PDF’s second-priority inclusion label is historical; assess current inheritance- and variant-specific evidence.|dcm2026|HCM evidence remains limited in the 2025 reappraisal. A DCM association must not be transferred to an HCM interpretation.

PKP2|AD|Arrhythmogenic CM;Ventricular arrhythmia|Plakophilin-2 helps assemble cardiac desmosomes. Pathogenic variants are an important cause of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy and related electrical disease.|Assess imaging, rhythm phenotype, and family history together; penetrance is variable and age-dependent.|acm|

PLN|AD; biallelic disease possible|DCM;Arrhythmogenic CM|Phospholamban regulates calcium reuptake into the sarcoplasmic reticulum. Certain pathogenic variants cause dilated or arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy.|Risk differs by variant. Avoid applying founder-variant outcome data to all PLN changes.|dcm|

PRKAG2|AD|Glycogen-storage CM;LVH;Pre-excitation;Conduction disease|The AMPK gamma-2 subunit regulates cellular energy sensing. PRKAG2 syndrome causes cardiac glycogen accumulation that can mimic HCM, often with pre-excitation and later conduction disease.|LVH plus a short PR interval or pre-excitation should prompt review for this HCM phenocopy.|hcm|

PTPN11|AD|Noonan spectrum;Pulmonary stenosis;HCM in selected syndromes|SHP2 regulates RAS-MAPK signaling. PTPN11 variants cause RASopathies, with cardiac findings that differ between Noonan syndrome and Noonan syndrome with multiple lentigines.|Assess dysmorphism, growth, lentigines, and congenital heart disease; syndrome-specific variant effects matter.|hcm|

RAF1|AD|Noonan spectrum;HCM|RAF1 is part of RAS-MAPK signaling. Certain activating variants cause Noonan-spectrum disease with a substantial association with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.|Consider syndromic assessment even when HCM dominates the presentation.|hcm|

RBM20|AD|DCM;Ventricular arrhythmia|RBM20 controls splicing of cardiac proteins, including titin. Pathogenic variants can cause dilated cardiomyopathy with prominent arrhythmic disease.|Variant location and functional mechanism matter; isolated HCM claims should be reviewed separately.|dcm|

RIT1|AD|Noonan syndrome;HCM|RIT1 regulates cellular signaling. Activating pathogenic variants cause a Noonan-spectrum disorder in which hypertrophic cardiomyopathy may be an early feature.|Review growth, facial features, congenital heart defects, and perinatal history.|hcm|

RYR2|AD; mechanism-dependent|CPVT;Calcium-release deficiency;Reported structural CM|The cardiac ryanodine receptor releases stored calcium for contraction. Gain-of-function variants typically cause CPVT; other mechanisms can cause distinct arrhythmic phenotypes.|Exercise or emotion-triggered syncope is a key clue. Source-panel overlap does not mean every RYR2 variant causes structural cardiomyopathy.|cpvt|Cardiac phenotype depends on mechanism; structural cardiomyopathy claims need separate evidence.

SCN5A|AD|Brugada syndrome;LQT3;Conduction disease;DCM|Nav1.5 carries the cardiac sodium current. Gain- and loss-of-function variants can produce different phenotypes, including long QT syndrome, Brugada syndrome, conduction disease, and some dilated cardiomyopathy.|Interpret the specific variant mechanism with the ECG and clinical context. Opposing channel effects cannot be assumed from the gene name.|lqts|

SGCD|AR for established sarcoglycanopathy|Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy;Cardiomyopathy|Delta-sarcoglycan stabilizes the muscle membrane. Biallelic pathogenic variants cause a muscular dystrophy that can involve the heart.|Look for muscle weakness and elevated CK. An isolated heterozygous finding needs cautious interpretation.|dcm|Established recessive muscle disease should not be conflated with a definitive dominant isolated DCM association.

TCAP|AR for established telethoninopathy|Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy;Reported cardiomyopathy|Telethonin contributes to sarcomere Z-disc assembly. Biallelic disease is associated with muscular dystrophy; proposed isolated cardiomyopathy associations have weaker support.|Review neuromuscular findings, zygosity, and the current gene-disease curation.|hcm|Isolated dominant HCM association is disputed in the 2025 reappraisal.

TNNC1|AD|HCM;DCM|Cardiac troponin C binds calcium to regulate contraction. Variant-specific changes in calcium sensitivity can cause hypertrophic or dilated cardiomyopathy.|The 2025 HCM reappraisal upgraded TNNC1 to definitive HCM validity.|hcm|

TNNI3|AD / AR|HCM;Restrictive CM;DCM|Cardiac troponin I inhibits actin-myosin interaction until calcium activation. Pathogenic variants can cause hypertrophic, restrictive, or dilated phenotypes.|Restrictive physiology with relatively little hypertrophy can be a useful clue; assess variant and inheritance.|hcm|

TNNT2|AD|HCM;DCM;Restrictive CM|Cardiac troponin T links the troponin complex to tropomyosin. Disease-associated variants affect calcium-regulated contraction and can produce multiple cardiomyopathy phenotypes.|Do not estimate sudden-death risk from the gene alone; integrate personal and family clinical findings.|hcm|

TPM1|AD|HCM;DCM;LV noncompaction|Alpha-tropomyosin regulates access of myosin to actin. Variant-specific effects on thin-filament regulation can cause hypertrophic or dilated disease.|Use the observed cardiac phenotype, variant mechanism, and segregation to guide interpretation.|hcm|

TTN|AD; AR in selected disorders|DCM;Skeletal myopathy|Titin provides sarcomere elasticity and structural support. Truncating variants in relevant cardiac-expressed exons are an important cause of dilated cardiomyopathy.|Exon usage, transcript, location, and variant class matter. Many rare missense variants remain uncertain.|dcm|Presence in the arrhythmia panel does not establish a primary channelopathy association.

TTR|AD|Hereditary ATTR amyloidosis;Infiltrative CM;Neuropathy|Transthyretin can form amyloid deposits in the heart and nerves. Hereditary ATTR amyloidosis is an important cause of increased ventricular wall thickness that can resemble HCM.|Distinguish variant from wild-type ATTR; coordinate amyloid evaluation and exclude light-chain disease as clinically indicated.|dcm|

VCL|AD; penetrance varies|DCM|Vinculin links cell adhesion complexes to the actin cytoskeleton. Selected pathogenic variants have been associated with dilated cardiomyopathy.|Interpret with segregation, phenotype, and current evidence; penetrance may be reduced.|dcm|Review current gene-disease validity and variant mechanism; not all rare VCL variants are causal.

CACNA1C|AD|Timothy syndrome;LQTS;Neurodevelopmental disease|Cav1.2 carries L-type calcium current. Variant-specific dysfunction can cause long QT and Timothy-spectrum disease, sometimes with syndactyly or neurodevelopmental features.|Distinguish syndromic CACNA1C disease from isolated LQTS; phenotype and mechanism change the interpretation.|lqts|Evidence for isolated LQTS differs from definitive syndromic disease; Brugada claims require separate review.

CACNB2|No established monogenic Brugada inheritance|Historical Brugada candidate|The calcium-channel beta-2 subunit regulates channel function. The PDF retains CACNB2 as a historical arrhythmia-panel gene, but biological plausibility is not proof of causation.|Prioritize validated disease genes and review expert curation before using a result clinically.|brugada|The ClinGen Brugada reappraisal classified non-SCN5A candidate genes, including CACNB2, as disputed.

CALM1|AD; often de novo|Early-onset LQTS;CPVT-like arrhythmia|Calmodulin senses calcium and controls cardiac ion channels. Pathogenic CALM1 variants can cause severe early-onset repolarization or calcium-triggered arrhythmia disorders.|Consider early presentation, marked QT prolongation, or exertional arrhythmia; evaluate variant-specific evidence.|lqts|

CALM2|AD; often de novo|Early-onset LQTS;CPVT-like arrhythmia|CALM2 encodes calmodulin, a calcium sensor essential for cardiac channel regulation. Pathogenic variants can cause severe childhood arrhythmia phenotypes.|A negative family history does not exclude a de novo calmodulinopathy.|lqts|

CALM3|AD; often de novo|Early-onset LQTS;Calmodulinopathy|CALM3 produces the same calmodulin protein as CALM1 and CALM2. Disruptive variants can impair channel regulation and cause severe early-onset arrhythmias.|Interpret the specific variant and clinical phenotype; the gene name alone does not establish severity.|lqts|

CASQ2|AR; AD for selected variants|CPVT|Calsequestrin-2 stores calcium inside the sarcoplasmic reticulum. Dysfunction can trigger adrenergically mediated ventricular arrhythmias, often with a normal resting ECG.|Biallelic disease is typical, but selected heterozygous variants can be relevant; assess zygosity and exercise phenotype.|cpvt|

GPD1L|No established monogenic Brugada inheritance|Historical Brugada candidate|GPD1L has been studied for effects on cardiac sodium-channel availability. It remains in the source list despite disputed evidence for monogenic Brugada causation.|Do not treat a rare GPD1L variant as a molecular diagnosis of Brugada syndrome.|brugada|Brugada gene-disease validity is disputed; panel retention is historical context.

HCN4|AD|Sinus bradycardia;Familial AF / tachycardia–bradycardia;LV noncompaction;Aortic dilation in some families|HCN4 carries a pacemaker current in the sinus node. Selected variants have been described in families with sinus-node dysfunction, tachycardia–bradycardia and atrial fibrillation. Some HCN4 families also have structural cardiac features.|Review resting rate, chronotropic response, atrial arrhythmias, imaging and family segregation. Interpret the specific variant and family phenotype; AF-focus placement does not exclude ventricular risk.|hcn4af|

KCNE1|AR for JLNS; AD context-dependent|Jervell and Lange-Nielsen;Acquired QT susceptibility|KCNE1 modulates the IKs potassium current. Biallelic pathogenic variants can cause long QT with congenital deafness; some alleles influence acquired QT susceptibility.|Separate biallelic syndromic disease from isolated dominant LQTS and medication-related susceptibility.|lqts|Monoallelic isolated congenital LQTS has limited evidence; a risk allele is not equivalent to a monogenic diagnosis.

KCNE2|Risk-allele context|Acquired QT susceptibility;Historical congenital LQTS candidate|KCNE2 modulates potassium-channel function. Certain alleles may influence susceptibility to acquired QT prolongation, but monogenic congenital LQTS causation is disputed.|Interpret drug and electrolyte context and the exact allele; avoid a congenital LQTS diagnosis based solely on this gene.|lqts|Congenital LQTS validity is disputed; susceptibility evidence addresses a different clinical question.

KCNH2|AD|LQT2;Short QT for selected variants|Kv11.1 carries the rapid delayed rectifier potassium current. Reduced current causes LQT2; different functional effects can cause other repolarization phenotypes.|Review QTc, T-wave morphology, medication exposure, electrolytes, and variant mechanism.|lqts|

KCNJ2|AD|Andersen-Tawil syndrome;Ventricular arrhythmia;Periodic paralysis|Kir2.1 contributes to the inward rectifier potassium current. Pathogenic variants can cause Andersen-Tawil syndrome with ventricular arrhythmia, periodic paralysis, and characteristic physical features.|Prominent U waves and bidirectional VT may be clues; distinguish the syndrome from isolated LQTS or typical CPVT.|lqts|Definitive syndromic disease is distinct from limited evidence for isolated congenital LQTS.

KCNQ1|AD / AR|LQT1;Jervell and Lange-Nielsen;Atrial arrhythmia|Kv7.1 carries the slow delayed rectifier potassium current. Loss-of-function variants cause LQT1; biallelic variants can cause long QT with congenital sensorineural deafness.|Consider exercise or swimming-triggered events, hearing status, zygosity, and the specific channel effect.|lqts|

TECRL|AR|CPVT;QT prolongation|TECRL-related disease disrupts cardiac calcium handling and can cause exercise- or emotion-triggered ventricular arrhythmias, sometimes with QT prolongation.|Confirm two pathogenic alleles in trans where relevant. An isolated heterozygous finding does not establish recessive CPVT.|cpvt|

TMEM43|AD|Arrhythmogenic CM|TMEM43 is associated with arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, particularly for well-characterized variants such as p.Ser358Leu.|Evidence and risk can be highly variant-specific; do not generalize founder-variant outcomes to every rare change.|acm|

TRDN|AR|CPVT;Triadin knockout syndrome;QT prolongation|Triadin organizes calcium-release complexes in the heart. Biallelic loss-of-function variants can cause severe childhood ventricular arrhythmias, sometimes with QT prolongation.|Confirm zygosity and phase. A single recessive allele generally requires further evaluation rather than a definitive diagnosis.|cpvt|

ACTA2|AD|Thoracic aortic disease;Occlusive arteriopathy|Smooth muscle alpha-actin supports arterial contraction. Pathogenic variants can cause heritable thoracic aneurysm and dissection, with extra-aortic vascular features in some individuals.|Review the entire vascular phenotype and family history; surveillance and intervention decisions require gene- and patient-specific assessment.|hta|

COL3A1|AD|Vascular Ehlers-Danlos;Arterial fragility|Type III collagen maintains vessel and hollow-organ integrity. Pathogenic variants cause vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, with arterial and organ fragility.|Consider easy bruising, translucent skin, and personal or family arterial/organ rupture; obtain specialist assessment.|hta|

COL5A1|AD|Classical Ehlers-Danlos|Type V collagen regulates collagen fibril assembly. Pathogenic variants typically cause classical Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, characterized by skin and joint findings.|Assess skin hyperextensibility, atrophic scars, and hypermobility; use syndrome-specific vascular interpretation.|hta|Classical EDS is not equivalent to definitive isolated HTAD; retained broad aortopathy-panel coverage.

COL5A2|AD|Classical Ehlers-Danlos|The alpha-2 chain of type V collagen contributes to connective tissue integrity. Pathogenic variants can cause classical Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.|Connect the result to skin, scar, and joint findings; evaluate the actual vascular phenotype separately.|hta|Evidence for classical EDS should not be presented as definitive isolated aortic disease validity.

EFEMP2|AR|Arterial tortuosity;Cutis laxa;Aneurysmal disease|Fibulin-4 is needed for elastic fiber formation. Biallelic disease can cause cutis laxa with marked arterial tortuosity, stenoses, and aneurysms.|Review systemic connective tissue features and establish biallelic status.|hta|

ELN|AD; mechanism-dependent|Supravalvular aortic stenosis;Cutis laxa|Elastin is a major component of arterial elastic fibers. Different variant mechanisms can cause obstructive arterial disease or autosomal dominant cutis laxa.|Distinguish haploinsufficiency-related stenosis from cutis-laxa mechanisms and associated vascular findings.|hta|Broad vascular-panel inclusion does not mean all ELN variants confer thoracic aneurysm risk.

FBN1|AD|Marfan syndrome;Aortic root aneurysm;Ectopia lentis|Fibrillin-1 forms extracellular microfibrils. Pathogenic variants can cause Marfan syndrome and related disorders with aortic, ocular, and skeletal involvement.|Integrate aortic root imaging, ocular findings, systemic assessment, and the variant mechanism.|hta|

FBN2|AD|Congenital contractural arachnodactyly|Fibrillin-2 supports elastic microfibril development. Pathogenic variants typically cause congenital contractural arachnodactyly with contractures and skeletal features.|Distinguish the contractural phenotype from Marfan syndrome; vascular interpretation should follow the specific diagnosis.|hta|The evidence base for isolated HTAD is less established than for FBN1.

FLNA|X-linked|Periventricular nodular heterotopia;Valve disease;Aortic dilation|Filamin-A connects actin to cellular signaling structures. Certain FLNA disorders combine neurodevelopmental, valvular, connective tissue, and aortic features.|Ask about seizures and neurological imaging; variant mechanism and sex affect the syndrome.|hta|

LOX|AD|Thoracic aortic aneurysm / dissection|Lysyl oxidase cross-links collagen and elastin. Pathogenic loss-of-function variants can weaken the aortic extracellular matrix and cause heritable thoracic aortic disease.|Assess family aortic history and obtain specialist gene-specific vascular review.|hta|

MYH11|AD|Thoracic aortic disease;Patent ductus arteriosus|Smooth muscle myosin heavy chain supports vascular contraction. Pathogenic variants can cause familial aortic disease, sometimes accompanied by patent ductus arteriosus.|Aortic disease plus a PDA in the family is a useful clue; variant mechanism needs review.|hta|

MYLK|AD for HTAD|Thoracic aortic dissection|Myosin light-chain kinase regulates smooth muscle contraction. Pathogenic variants can cause aortic dissection, sometimes without marked preceding dilation.|Family dissection history and gene-specific specialist assessment are important; diameter alone may not capture risk.|hta|

NOTCH1|AD|Bicuspid aortic valve;Aortic valve disease|NOTCH1 signaling is important for cardiovascular development. Pathogenic variants can cause left-sided congenital heart disease, including bicuspid aortic valve.|Interpret alongside valve anatomy and family history; assess aortic findings on their own merits.|hta|Congenital valve disease validity differs from limited evidence for isolated HTAD.

PRKG1|AD|Thoracic aortic aneurysm / dissection|Protein kinase G regulates smooth muscle relaxation. Selected activating variants can cause familial aortic disease and dissection.|Review the specific gain-of-function mechanism; do not apply known high-risk variant data to every rare change.|hta|

SKI|AD|Shprintzen-Goldberg syndrome;Connective tissue disease|SKI regulates developmental signaling. Pathogenic variants cause Shprintzen-Goldberg syndrome with craniosynostosis, skeletal features, and possible aortic involvement.|Look for the syndromic phenotype and seek connective tissue/genetics assessment.|hta|

SLC2A10|AR|Arterial tortuosity syndrome|GLUT10-related disease affects connective tissue and arterial integrity. Biallelic variants can cause generalized arterial tortuosity with stenoses and aneurysms.|Confirm biallelic status and review the wider arterial tree and systemic connective tissue phenotype.|hta|

SMAD2|AD|Loeys-Dietz spectrum;Arterial aneurysm / tortuosity|SMAD2 transmits TGF-beta signals. Disease-associated variants can cause a connective tissue disorder with arterial aneurysm, tortuosity, and variable syndromic features.|Use the exact gene-disease pair and specialist vascular assessment; expression varies within families.|hta|

SMAD3|AD|Loeys-Dietz spectrum;Aneurysm-osteoarthritis syndrome|SMAD3 is a TGF-beta signaling mediator. Pathogenic variants can cause widespread arterial disease, often with early osteoarthritis.|Early joint degeneration alongside aortic or other arterial disease is a useful diagnostic clue.|hta|

SMAD4|AD|Juvenile polyposis / HHT;Variable aortic involvement|SMAD4 integrates TGF-beta signaling. Certain variants cause juvenile polyposis with hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, with aortic involvement reported in some affected individuals.|Review GI polyps, bleeding, telangiectasia, and AVMs; variant mechanism distinguishes other SMAD4 syndromes.|hta|This is syndrome-oriented coverage, not equivalent evidence for isolated HTAD.

TGFB2|AD|Loeys-Dietz spectrum;Thoracic aortic disease|TGF-beta-2 participates in extracellular matrix regulation and vascular development. Pathogenic variants can cause heritable aortic disease with variable connective tissue features.|Review aortic and extra-aortic arterial findings and the family phenotype.|hta|

TGFB3|AD|Loeys-Dietz spectrum;Thoracic aortic disease|TGF-beta-3 signaling supports vascular and connective tissue homeostasis. Disease-associated variants can produce heritable thoracic aortic disease with variable syndromic features.|The PDF places this addition in a second-priority extension; seek current gene-specific expert guidance.|hta|Outcome data and disease validity are less extensive than for core HTAD genes; the GeneReviews overview lists limited HTAD evidence.

TGFBR1|AD|Loeys-Dietz syndrome;Arterial aneurysm / tortuosity|TGF-beta receptor type 1 participates in vascular developmental signaling. Pathogenic variants can cause Loeys-Dietz syndrome and heritable aortic disease.|Assess extra-aortic arterial and systemic features; use specialist gene-specific surveillance and intervention guidance.|hta|

TGFBR2|AD|Loeys-Dietz syndrome;Thoracic aortic disease|TGF-beta receptor type 2 participates in extracellular matrix and vascular regulation. Pathogenic variants can cause aortic and more widespread arterial disease.|Evaluate the syndromic phenotype, family history, and extra-aortic vasculature with an experienced team.|hta|

ACVRL1|AD|HHT type 2;PAH|ALK1 is an endothelial BMP/TGF-beta pathway receptor. Pathogenic variants cause hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia and can be associated with pulmonary arterial hypertension.|Distinguish true pulmonary vascular disease from high-output pulmonary hypertension related to HHT vascular malformations.|pah|

ATP13A3|AD / AR; dosage-dependent|Heritable PAH;Early severe PAH|ATP13A3 participates in polyamine transport and endothelial homeostasis. Pathogenic variants can cause PAH, with more severe early disease reported in biallelic individuals.|Assess allele dosage and family history; incomplete penetrance affects counseling.|pah|

BMPR2|AD|Heritable PAH|BMPR-II transmits BMP signals needed for pulmonary vascular homeostasis. Pathogenic variants are a major cause of heritable PAH with incomplete penetrance.|Offer specialist genetic counseling and family risk assessment after a confirmed pathogenic result.|pah|

CAV1|AD; other inheritance in distinct disorders|Heritable PAH;Lipodystrophy in selected disorders|Caveolin-1 organizes endothelial membrane caveolae and signaling. Selected pathogenic variants are associated with pulmonary arterial hypertension.|Interpret the allele and disease mechanism; lipodystrophy associations involve different clinical contexts.|pah|

EIF2AK4|AR|PVOD / PCH|GCN2 regulates the cellular stress response. Biallelic pathogenic variants cause heritable pulmonary veno-occlusive disease / pulmonary capillary hemangiomatosis, which can resemble PAH.|PVOD/PCH needs expert distinction from PAH; pulmonary vasodilators can provoke pulmonary edema in this setting.|pah|

ENG|AD|HHT type 1;Pulmonary vascular disease|Endoglin is an endothelial BMP/TGF-beta co-receptor. Pathogenic variants cause HHT, with vascular malformations and pulmonary vascular complications.|Assess epistaxis, telangiectasia, and AVMs; distinguish high-output or shunt-related disease from PAH.|pah|

GDF2|AD / AR; phenotype-dependent|PAH;Vascular malformation spectrum|BMP9 is a circulating ligand in pulmonary endothelial signaling. Disease-associated variants can impair vascular homeostasis and cause PAH or related vascular phenotypes.|Review zygosity, functional effect, and the exact vascular presentation.|pah|

KCNK3|AD; biallelic severe disease reported|Heritable PAH|TASK-1 is a potassium channel that helps set pulmonary arterial smooth muscle membrane potential. Loss-of-function can promote pulmonary vascular disease.|Assess inheritance and variant function; the finding requires a pulmonary hypertension phenotype and expert classification.|pah|

KDR|AD|PAH;Low diffusion capacity|VEGFR2 supports vascular endothelial signaling. Pathogenic loss-of-function variants have been associated with PAH, sometimes with reduced pulmonary diffusion capacity.|Review DLCO, pulmonary imaging, and phenotype-specific variant evidence.|pah|

SMAD9|AD|Heritable PAH|SMAD9 transmits BMP pathway signals. Disease-associated variants can disrupt pulmonary vascular signaling and contribute to heritable PAH.|Consider reduced penetrance and use specialist counseling for family assessment.|pah|

SOX17|AD|PAH;Congenital heart disease|SOX17 is a transcription factor important for endothelial development. Pathogenic variants are associated with PAH, including pediatric disease with congenital heart defects.|Review congenital cardiac anatomy and family history alongside the pulmonary vascular diagnosis.|pah|

TBX4|AD|PAH;Small patella syndrome;Developmental lung disease|TBX4 directs limb and lung development. Pathogenic variants can cause PAH with skeletal clues or developmental lung abnormalities, particularly in childhood.|Examine patellae, pelvis, and feet, and review lung development; skeletal findings may be subtle.|pah|

ABCG5|AR|Sitosterolemia;Premature ASCVD;Xanthomas|ABCG5 works with ABCG8 to export plant sterols. Biallelic loss-of-function causes sitosterolemia, an important familial hypercholesterolemia mimic.|Consider plasma plant sterols when xanthomas, premature ASCVD, or hematologic abnormalities suggest sitosterolemia.|lipid|

ABCG8|AR|Sitosterolemia;Premature ASCVD;Xanthomas|ABCG8 pairs with ABCG5 to limit sterol absorption and promote excretion. Biallelic disease causes sitosterolemia with variable cholesterol elevation.|Plant sterol measurement can distinguish this disorder from conventional familial hypercholesterolemia.|lipid|

APOB|AD; mechanism-dependent|Familial hypercholesterolemia;Hypobetalipoproteinemia|Apolipoprotein B is the principal structural protein of LDL. Specific receptor-binding defects can cause familial hypercholesterolemia; other variant classes cause low LDL instead.|Interpret against the lipid profile and mechanism; not every APOB variant raises LDL cholesterol.|lipid|

APOE|Allele- and context-dependent|Dysbetalipoproteinemia;Rare dominant hypercholesterolemia|Apolipoprotein E mediates remnant lipoprotein clearance. Specific genotypes or variants can predispose to dysbetalipoproteinemia or rare dominant hypercholesterolemia.|Use genotype-specific interpretation with cholesterol, triglycerides, and secondary factors; this panel is not an Alzheimer risk assessment.|lipid|Common APOE alleles have context-dependent effects and are not interchangeable with monogenic FH variants.
